record.excerpt: Rule 2: Don't Buy Until There's a Dip Greater Than 5% from the Most Recent High Price … The DCA case assumed our investor spent $1 on Bitcoin every day from May 1, 2013 until May 23, 2021 … $1/Day – >5% Dips (Rule 2) | $2943 | 4.639 … $1/Day – >10% Dips (Rule 3) | $2943 | 4.42 … the data is clear: dollar cost averaging works better than buying the dip.
record.performance_claim: dollar cost averaging works better than buying the dip
record.notes: Accumulation rule (save $1/day, deploy on >5%/>10% dip from recent high) vs daily DCA; a negative claim, nice contrast. Bold markers removed from table cells.

spec.claim_summary: Waiting to buy bitcoin only when price is more than 5% below the most recent high underperforms daily dollar-cost averaging.
spec.untestable_reason: Rule 2 requires buying on every day price is more than 5% below the recent high and holding all lots, which is a DCA/pyramiding accumulation the single-position engine cannot express.
assumptions: Asset is Bitcoin mapped to BTCUSDT.
Timeframe 1d chosen as most natural reading for daily purchase cadence; claim states no bar timeframe.
Most Recent High Price has no lookback stated; approximated as 90-day highest_high for closest testable core.
Dip Greater Than 5% encoded as close < 0.95 * highest_high for closest testable core.
No exit stated; Rule 2 holds all lots with no sale, so closest core has no exit.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: repeated $1 purchases on every dip day and holding all lots as a DCA ladder / pyramiding / position sizing accumulation; single-position engine holds one position at a time so repeated dip buying cannot be tested.

issues.problem: Spec holds a single position to end (empty exit + max_hold_bars 5000) after first >5% dip. Claim's Rule 2 buys on every dip day ('Don't Buy Until There's a Dip Greater Than 5% from the Most Recent High Price' with same $2943 total) and holds all lots. Single-entry encoding prevents repeated dip purchases and tests a one-time timing trade, not the accumulation rule.
